'''Margaret Bunting Wyman Tent''' (born '''Margaret Bunting Wyman'''; November 2, 1944 – September 20, 2014), also known by her [[pen name]] '''M. B. W. Tent''', was an American mathematics educator and writer. She was the author of several bestselling books.

== Life ==
Tent was born in [[Westfield, Massachusetts]] and grew up in [[Amherst, Massachusetts]].<ref name="obituary">{{cite news |title=Margaret Tent |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/113492724/margaret-tent-m-b-w-tent-obituary/ |newspaper=[[Daily Hampshire Gazette]] |date=September 24, 2014 |page=B2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |access-date=November 22, 2022}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://ubiquity.acm.org/article.cfm?id=1238610|title=Ubiquity: Review of 'The Prince of Mathematics: Carl Friedrich Gauss' by M.B.W. Tent, A.K. Peters, Ltd., 2006|website=ubiquity.acm.org|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref>  She worked as a teacher at Altamont high school in Birmingham, Alabama beginning in 1985.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=http://www.bokus.com/bok/9781568814308/emmy-noether/|title=Emmy Noether av M B W Tent (Bok)|isbn=9781568814308|language=sv|last1=Tent|first1=M. B. W.|date=2008-10-10|publisher=Taylor & Francis }}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2010, she and her husband moved to [[Frederick, Maryland]] to retire from teaching and continue writing.<ref name="obituary"/>

On September 20, 2014 she died of [[breast cancer]] at a [[hospice]] in [[Mount Airy, Maryland]] at age 69.<ref name="obituary"/>

== Career ==
Tent attended [[Amherst Regional High School (Massachusetts)|Amherst Regional High School]]<ref name=":1" /> and is a graduate of [[Mount Holyoke College]].<ref name=":0" />  She received her bachelor's and master's degree from the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham|University of Alabama, Birmingham]].<ref name=":1" />

Before teaching post-secondary education, she taught adult education at business colleges and for two years for the American Military in Berlin, Germany.<ref name="obituary"/>

She has been teaching and writing about mathematics for many years.<ref name=":0" />

== Critical reception ==
Most of her books have received good reviews from organizations such as the [[Mathematical Association of America]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/publications/periodicals/convergence/the-prince-of-mathematics-carl-friedrich-gauss|title=The Prince of Mathematics: Carl Friedrich Gauss {{!}} Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org|language=en|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref> [[Association for Computing Machinery]] and [[Goodreads]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.goodreads.com/author/show/435059.M_B_W_Tent|title=M.B.W. Tent|website=www.goodreads.com|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref>

Her books have received hundreds of citations in the academic press.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Reviewer-Gagliano|first=Ross|date=2007-03-01|title=Review of 'The Prince of Mathematics: Carl Friedrich Gauss' by M.B.W. Tent, A.K. Peters, Ltd., 2006|url=http://dl.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=1232048.1238610|journal=Ubiquity|volume=2007|issue=March|pages=3|doi=10.1145/1232048.1238610|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Her books have also received praise from other authors and mathematicians like [[William Dunham (mathematician)|William Dunham]], [[Peter Lax]], [[Cathleen Synge Morawetz]], [[Charles Ashbacher]] and [[Peter M. Neumann]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhbs.com/the_prince_of_mathematics_tefno_162101.html|title=The Prince of Mathematics: Carl Friedrich Gauss|website=www.nhbs.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Some of her best known works are:<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/s?ie=UTF8&field-author=M.%20B.%20W.%20Tent&page=1&rh=n:283155,p_27:M.%20B.%20W.%20Tent|title=Amazon.com: M. B. W. Tent: Books|website=www.amazon.com|access-date=2018-03-15}}</ref>

* ''[[Emmy Noether: The Mother of Modern Algebra]]'' [https://books.google.com/books?id=RmY_Cq9MNCcC]
* ''Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz: The Polymath Who Brought Us Calculus'' [https://books.google.com/books?id=puSYtSk0POUC&dq=mbw+tent&pg=PR4]
* ''[[Leonhard Euler and the Bernoullis: Mathematicians from Basel]]'' [https://books.google.com/books?id=TZskvTzKzTUC]
